objective: Frozen exploratory census over the block removals of the Z3 lift (one law per symmetry class), the two lifts of the shadow K6, two disjoint unions (parity beside J; K4 beside the Z3 law) and controls (Z6, the Boolean neither-knot, parity, the Z3 law). For each law: elimination on random systems; for laws without a failure, candidate tops from observed reflexive relations, hidden circuits under the top blur, bijective tie images, functional knot images, and a solver search for a ternary polymorphism Mal'tsev modulo the tops on the knot ranges found and on all ranges found.
status: Closed: supported by CYCLE-TOPS-20261021-001A-E001 (exploratory; H1-H6 hold and all four controls pass; the independent check re-verified all 43 failures by brute force, every operation table and top certificate, and replicated the counts on 400 fresh systems per surviving law; its first version named block classes by their first member instead of their least image and compared certificate blocks in recorded order, and both bookkeeping errors were corrected before it passed). Of the 46 classes of removals from the (2,2,2)-block of the Z3 lift, exactly five have no failure in 6000 systems: nothing, (2,2,2), (2,2,3), {223,232} and the whole one-3 class {223,232,322}; all are dressed. Both lifts of K6 and both disjoint unions (parity beside J, K4 beside Z3) have no failure. In every surviving law no circuit hides below the candidate tops, every tie's top image is a bijection and every knot's top image is functional. Every surviving law has a ternary polymorphism Mal'tsev modulo the tops on its knot ranges; on all ranges the two unions have none, because their whole-domain top is certified equality and J and K4 are not rectangular. Z6 fails, its mod-2 and mod-3 relations join to the total relation, and the mod-2 blur frees its mod-3 tie.
title: Census: tops near the known families
